question:
For a given list of input numbers, calculate Mean Absolute Deviation around the mean of this dataset. Mean Absolute Deviation is the average absolute difference between each element and a centerpoint (mean in this case): MAD = average | x - x_mean |

Implement the solution in Racket.
Use `#lang racket`.
Define the function `mean_absolute_deviation`.
When the original task refers to Python lists or tuples, use Racket lists.
Preserve the original task semantics.
Return only valid Racket code.
answer:
#lang racket

(define (mean_absolute_deviation lst)
  (let* ((mean (/ (apply + lst) (length lst)))
         (diffs (map (lambda (x) (abs (- x mean))) lst)))
    (/ (apply + diffs) (length diffs))))

answer:
#lang racket
(define (intersperse lst delimiter)
  (if (null? lst)
      '()
      (cons (car lst)
            (if (null? (cdr lst))
                '()
                (cons delimiter (intersperse (cdr lst) delimiter))))))

#lang racket

(define (filter_by_substring lst substr)
  (filter (lambda (str) (string-contains? str substr)) lst))

(define (rolling_max lst)
  (letrec ((helper (lambda (lst max_lst max_elem)
                     (cond ((null? lst) max_lst)
                           (else (helper (cdr lst) (cons (max max_elem (car lst)) max_lst) (max max_elem (car lst))))))))
    (reverse (helper lst '() (if (null? lst) '() (car lst))))))

(define (find-suffix s len)

    (if (or (= i 0) (palindrome? (substring s 0 i)))

(define (palindrome? s)

    (or (= len 0) (= len 1)
        (and (char=? (string-ref s 0) (string-ref s (- len 1)))

Find the shortest palindrome that begins with a supplied string. Algorithm idea is simple: - Find the longest postfix of supplied string that is a palindrome. - Append to the end of the string reverse of a string prefix that comes before the palindromic suffix.

Implement the solution in Racket.
Use `#lang racket`.
Define the function `make_palindrome`.
When the original task refers to Python lists or tuples, use Racket lists.
Preserve the original task semantics.
Return only valid Racket code.

(define (make_palindrome s)
  (let* ((len (string-length s))
         (suffix (find-suffix s len))
         (prefix (substring s 0 (- len (string-length suffix)))))
    (string-append s (reverse-string prefix))))

(define (find-suffix s len)
  (let loop ((i len))
    (if (or (= i 0) (palindrome? (substring s 0 i)))
      (substring s 0 i)
      (loop (- i 1)))))

(define (palindrome? s)
  (let ((len (string-length s)))
    (or (= len 0) (= len 1)
        (and (char=? (string-ref s 0) (string-ref s (- len 1)))
             (palindrome? (substring s 1 (- len 1)))))))

(define (reverse-string s)
  (list->string (reverse (string->list s))))

Input are two strings a and b consisting only of 1s and 0s. Perform binary XOR on these inputs and return result also as a string.

Implement the solution in Racket.
Use `#lang racket`.
Define the function `string_xor`.
When the original task refers to Python lists or tuples, use Racket lists.

Return only valid Racket code.
answer:
#lang racket

(define (string_xor a b)
  (let ([len (min (string-length a) (string-length b))])
    (apply string-append
           (map (lambda (x y)
                  (if (equal? x y)
                      "0"
                      "1"))
                (take (string->list a) len)
                (take (string->list b) len)))))

#lang racket

(define (all_prefixes str)
  (let ((len (string-length str)))
    (let prefix-loop ((i 1))
      (if (> i len)
          '()
          (cons (substring str 0 i) (prefix-loop (+ i 1)))))))

Find how many times a given substring can be found in the original string. Count overlaping cases.

Implement the solution in Racket.
Use `#lang racket`.
Define the function `how_many_times`.
When the original task refers to Python lists or tuples, use Racket lists.
Preserve the original task semantics.
Return only valid Racket code.
answer:
#lang racket
(define (how_many_times s sub)
  (letrec ([count (lambda (s sub c)
                    (cond
                      [(< (string-length s) (string-length sub)) c]
                      [(string=? (substring s 0 (string-length sub)) sub)
                       (count (substring s 1 (string-length s)) sub (+ c 1))]
                      [else (count (substring s 1 (string-length s)) sub c)]))])
    (count s sub 0)))
